whatIsTale.a: Tale is an open-source, self-hosted platform that orchestrates AI agents: it connects the agents and CLIs your team already uses, pools their knowledge into one governed knowledge base, and runs automations with human approval — on your own infrastructure or in a managed cloud in Switzerland or the EU.

openSource.a: Yes. Tale is MIT-licensed and the full feature set ships in the free Community edition — Enterprise adds support and services, not features.

onPrem.q: Can Tale run fully on-premises or air-gapped?
onPrem.a: Yes. Tale self-hosts on your VPC, on-premises hardware, or fully air-gapped environments; with local models, no data ever leaves your network.

enterprisePricing.a: Enterprise is billed per user/month, with two months free when paying yearly. Storage beyond the included quota is billed per TB/month. The Community edition stays free for self-hosted use.

enterpriseFeatures.q: Are there additional features in the Enterprise plan?
enterpriseFeatures.a: No. All product features are available in the open source version too. Enterprise adds extended support and services.

byoModels.q: Do I have to bring my own AI models?
byoModels.a: No. You can bring your own models, but it's not required. Tale supports most major AI providers without markup — cloud model usage is billed at your provider's rates and is not included in the plans.

aiProviders.q: Can I use my preferred AI provider?
aiProviders.a: Yes. Tale supports the major cloud AI providers without markup — usage is billed at your provider's rates, so you keep your vendor and your existing billing.

hardware.a: Yes — hardware is available on rental, leasing, or purchase terms. Mention it when you contact the team and you'll get a quote for the configuration that fits.

ownHardwareModels.q: Can I use my own hardware and AI models?
ownHardwareModels.a: Yes. Tale is hardware- and model-agnostic, so you're free to use your own.

customTraining.q: Do you offer custom AI model training?
customTraining.a: Yes. Custom model training and fine-tuning are available for clients. Bring it up in the demo call if you need it.

platformAgents.description: A Tale agent is the four-knob combination of instructions, knowledge, tools, and a model. Editors build them once; the team runs them in chat, automations, and projects — including external agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini.

capabilities.heading: What can agents do?
capabilities.description: What one agent definition gives the whole team — and what it adds beyond a bare model.

items.title: Four knobs, one unit
items.body: Instructions, knowledge, tools, and model define how an agent behaves. Change one knob without re-training anything.

items.title: External agents dock in
items.body: Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini so work routes to the agent that already lives in your stack.

items.title: Delegation between agents
items.body: Specialist agents hand work to each other when a thread leaves one domain — without losing the transcript.

items.title: Skills as reusable bundles
items.body: Package a writing voice or multi-step pattern once and bind it to up to ten agents.

items.title: Knowledge scoped per agent
items.body: Each agent searches only the library slices you grant — team docs stay invisible outside the team.

items.q: What is an agent in Tale?
items.a: A Tale agent combines instructions, knowledge, tools, and a model into one reusable unit that Members run in chat and automations.

items.q: Can Tale orchestrate Claude Code and Cursor?
items.a: Yes. Tale connects external agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini so your team routes work through one orchestrator.

items.q: When should I use an agent instead of a workflow?
items.a: Use an agent when the conversation stays in one domain and voice. Reach for an automation when the work needs multiple steps, branches, schedules, or approvals.

items.q: Can each agent use a different model?
items.a: Yes. Every agent binds its own primary model and fallbacks — Claude Code can run on Claude Opus while a support specialist runs Claude Sonnet. Swap the model without rebuilding the agent.

items.q: What is Chat in Tale?
items.a: Tale Chat is the everyday surface where you pick an agent, send a message, and read a streamed reply with citations and tool calls.

items.q: Does Chat work without an agent?
items.a: Yes. Raw chat uses the model's defaults when you are exploring; reach for an agent when the same question will recur.

items.q: What is Arena mode?
items.a: Arena mode runs the same prompt against more than one model or agent so you can compare replies before you choose.

items.q: Can Chat take actions, or only answer?
items.a: Both. When a reply would call an integration or start a workflow, the action pauses on an in-chat approval card first — right where the work is happening.

platformAutomations.title: What are Automations in Tale?
platformAutomations.description: An automation bundles integrations, agents, a workflow, and the views it ships — an Inbox, for example — into one installable unit. The workflow inside is a graph of typed steps — LLM, Action, Condition, Loop, Sandbox — with schedules, webhooks, events, and human approvals.

capabilities.heading: What ships in an automation?
capabilities.description: Compose multi-step work as a typed graph — LLM, action, condition, loop, and sandbox steps — with approvals and versioned runs.

items.title: Installable bundles
items.body: Owners and Admins install from the catalog; Members use the Inbox, agents, or views it registers without assembling pieces by hand.

items.title: Typed workflow steps
items.body: LLM, Action, Condition, Loop, and Sandbox steps compose the graph. Every save snapshots a version you can restore.

items.title: Triggers that fit the job
items.body: Schedules (cron), webhooks, platform events, or a manual test run from the editor.

items.title: Execution logs
items.body: Every run records status, timing, inputs, and a per-step journal — audit trail and debugger in one place.

items.title: Approvals in the loop
items.body: Proposed workflow edits, agent-started runs, and waiting-for-input pauses land as approval cards before work continues.

items.q: What is an automation in Tale?
items.a: A Tale automation is an installable bundle — integrations, agents, a workflow, and ready-made views like an Inbox — that runs multi-step work with triggers and approvals.

items.q: Is there a standalone workflow product?
items.a: No. A workflow lives inside its automation. The automation's Editor tab is where you meet the graph.

items.q: When should I use an automation instead of an agent?
items.a: Use an automation when the job needs multiple steps, branches, schedules, or approvals between them — not when a single conversational agent is enough.

items.q: Can I test a workflow before it runs on a schedule?
items.a: Yes. The editor has a manual test run — you watch a complete execution with inputs, a per-step journal, and timing before any trigger goes live.

items.q: What is Knowledge in Tale?
items.a: Tale Knowledge is the org's shared library of documents, facts, websites, and typed records that agents retrieve and cite in replies.

items.q: Do agents see the whole library by default?
items.a: No. Each agent's Knowledge tab sets retrieval scope. Team-scoped items stay invisible outside the team.

items.q: What is the difference between documents and typed records?
items.a: Documents and entries are indexed for retrieval. Products, Customers, and Vendors are structured rows agents read as exact values.

items.q: Can agents write to Knowledge, or only read?
items.a: They can propose. Entries captured from a chat pause on an approval card; a person decides what enters the library, and the decision is logged.

platformGovernance.title: What is Governance in Tale?
platformGovernance.description: Governance is the seam between agent initiative and human judgement: approval cards hold actions until someone decides, every decision lands in the audit log, and spend stays visible — without a separate approver inbox.

capabilities.heading: What does governance cover?
capabilities.description: Put a human in the loop where it matters — with an audit trail, budget controls, and filters that keep sensitive data out of prompts and replies.

items.title: In-chat approval cards
items.body: Plans, document writes, knowledge writes, integration calls, MCP tools, and workflow runs pause until approve or reject.

items.title: Suggest changes on integrations
items.body: Describe what is wrong; the agent revises the call instead of abandoning the work.

items.title: Audit trail
items.body: Each decision records actor, action, and timestamp. Resolved cards stay in the transcript.

items.title: Guardrails and policies
items.body: Org-level guardrails and the run-code policy set the limits on what agents may attempt — before a card ever appears.

items.title: PII filtered in both directions
items.body: Every chat message passes content safety, PII detection, and an optional moderation provider — on the way in and the way out. Matches block, mask, or flag; the matched text itself is never stored.

items.title: Usage visibility
items.body: Usage analytics and budgets keep model spend visible to Admins.

items.q: What is Governance in Tale?
items.a: Tale Governance holds agent actions behind in-chat approval cards, writes decisions to the audit log, and keeps usage visible to Admins.

items.q: Is there a separate approval inbox?
items.a: No. Approvals are decided in the conversation they interrupt, by whoever holds that chat.

items.q: Can I choose which actions require approval?
items.a: Yes. Approvals are configurable per action type — plans, document and knowledge writes, integration calls, MCP tools, and workflow runs can each require a human decision before they run.

items.q: Can agents send email without approval?
items.a: Not if you require approval for it. Outbound actions hold as in-chat cards until someone decides — you choose which action types need a decision.

items.q: How does Tale help with GDPR and PII?
items.a: Keep processing on infrastructure you control, let PII detection mask personal data before it reaches or leaves a model, and point auditors at the audit log. Tale is GDPR-compliant, certified to ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, and publishes its DPA and technical and organizational measures.

items.q: What are Conversations in Tale?
items.a: Tale Conversations are shared chat threads your team can resume, with history, handoffs, and attached approval records.

items.q: How is this different from Chat?
items.a: Chat is the everyday composer surface. Conversations names the shared, durable thread layer teams hand off and resume.

items.q: Can I hand a conversation to a teammate or another agent?
items.a: Yes. A shared thread keeps its full history, so a person or a specialist agent can pick it up without losing context — and governance stays attached to every action.

items.q: Does the whole team see every conversation?
items.a: No — projects scope who sees what. A thread lives in its workspace, and only that workspace's members can read or resume it.
